name: Domaine Huet Vouvray Demi-Sec Le Mont 2015
text:
## Domaine Huet Vouvray Demi-Sec Le Mont 2015

**The story.** Domaine Huet is the most celebrated wine estate in [Vouvray](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Domaine+Huet,+11+Rue+de+la+Croix+Buis%C3%A9e,+Vouvray,+France&t=k), just east of [Tours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tours) in the [Loire Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loire_Valley_%28wine%29); Wikipedia calls it the most celebrated producer of the whole Loire, and the only one to have headlined a [Christie's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christie's) auction ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domaine_Huet)). Victor Huet, a Parisian bistro owner, and his son Gaston fell for the property while passing through Vouvray in 1928 and bought it the same year, with just five hectares of vines ([Domaine Huet](https://www.domainehuet.com/?lang=EN); [Benchmark Wine](https://www.benchmarkwine.com/products/63324-huet-vouvray-le-mont-moelleux-premiere-trie-2015)). After Gaston's death in 2002 the domaine was sold to pay French inheritance tax; the Hwang family, owners of Hungary's [Királyudvar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokaji) Tokaji estate, bought it in 2003, and Gaston's son-in-law Noël Pinguet stayed on as winemaker until 2012 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domaine_Huet)).

Huet was one of the pioneers of [biodynamic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodynamic_agriculture) farming in French vineyards, with vineyard work guided by the rhythms of the planets, "as winegrowers of past centuries did, more or less consciously" ([Domaine Huet](https://www.domainehuet.com/?lang=EN)). Everything is [Chenin Blanc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chenin_blanc), known locally as Pineau de la Loire and, more poetically, as "Plan du Clair de Lune", the moonlight vine.

**The three vineyards.** Huet farms 30 hectares in three parcels, each bottled separately ([Domaine Huet](https://www.domainehuet.com/?lang=EN); [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domaine_Huet)):
- **Le Haut-Lieu** (15 ha, bought 1928), the original vineyard on the plateau, with deep brown clay: fruity and fresh wines.
- **Clos du Bourg** (6 ha, bought 1953), one of the oldest vineyards in Vouvray, above the village church and enclosed by an ancient stone wall the estate dates to the 9th century; shallow clay and limestone over [tuffeau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuffeau_stone). Its wines are deep and dense. Gaston Huet considered it the finest vineyard in the appellation ([Lebendige Weine](https://www.lebendigeweine.de/en/le-clos-du-bourg-demi-sec-2017-huet/)).
- **Le Mont** (9 ha, bought 1957), on the south-facing first slope directly above Huet's tuffeau cellars, with stony soil and green clay. Its wines are "chiselled", fresh and mineral, often carried by very fine acidity.

**Vouvray styles.** In Vouvray the weather decides the style. Cooler years make dry (sec) and sparkling wines; warmer ones bring sweet moelleux, sometimes concentrated by [noble rot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noble_rot) as in [Sauternes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauternes_%28wine%29). Thanks to Chenin's natural acidity, the best can age for decades: a few drink well at 100, but more typically they peak around 40 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vouvray_%28wine%29)). Huet makes sec, demi-sec (off-dry) and moelleux (sweet) from each vineyard, and in great years a Première Trie, from the first and most selective pass through the vines.

**The wine.** This is Huet's off-dry (demi-sec) Chenin Blanc from Le Mont, the stony, green-clay first slope above the cellars, whose wines the estate describes as "chiselled", fresh and mineral, carried by fine acidity ([Domaine Huet](https://www.domainehuet.com/?lang=EN)). Stephan Reinhardt calls Le Mont's pebbly silex and green clay "probably the most exciting soil for the off-dry style" ([JJ Buckley](https://www.jjbuckley.com/wine/2016-domaine-huet-vouvray-le-mont-demi-sec/2016-12238-750/)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [Loire Valley vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/loire-valley) calls 2015 "very promising across the region", with the same warm, dry summer much of France enjoyed. [Touraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touraine), which includes Vouvray, had very low yields but excellent quality, and Chenin Blanc "fared well, with the potential to make good wine at all sweetness levels".

**What the critics say for 2015.**
- **Falstaff: 93** (Benjamin Herzog and Dominik Vombach, May 2021, [Falstaff](https://www.falstaff.com/en/wines/domaine-huet-2015-vouvray-aoc-le-mont-demi-sec)). Bright golden yellow; ripe yellow tropical fruit, quince and honey, fine minerality and a slight smoky touch, ripe peach; juicy, complex and elegant, with pineapple and honey, integrated sweetness, and a fresher, drier, saltier finish. Falstaff's Peter Moser had also given it 93 in 2019.
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 91.8** (from your CellarTracker list).
- (I couldn't read other critics' notes for the 2015 Le Mont demi-sec, so I've left them out.)

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is eleven years old. A ripe vintage, it was already showing honey and tropical fruit at six; now it should be gaining honeyed, waxy depth while the acidity keeps it fresh. Decant 30 minutes and serve at 10 to 12°C; it has many years ahead.

**Serving.** Serve Huet cool but not icy, about 10 to 12°C, in a white wine glass with room to swirl. Young bottles can show a flinty, struck-match note that blows off with air, so open them half an hour ahead, or even decant. Once opened, Huet keeps well in the fridge for several days.

**Food.** Demi-sec Vouvray is one of the most food-friendly wines there is. A German merchant suggests sweetbreads with morels and asparagus, skate wing with capers, or a pear and almond tart ([Lebendige Weine](https://www.lebendigeweine.de/en/le-clos-du-bourg-demi-sec-2017-huet/)). My picks: roast pork or chicken with apples and cream, spicy Thai or Sichuan dishes, scallops with brown butter, or a [rillettes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rillette) of [Tours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tours) on toast. Sweeter moelleux suits [foie gras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foie_gras), blue cheese like [Roquefort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roquefort), or an apple [tarte Tatin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarte_Tatin).

**Value and where to buy.** None of the three stores on this site lists Huet at the moment. It turns up with fine-wine merchants and at auction, and for wines of this pedigree and longevity it is remarkably good value.

**From the history books**
- **Monks and Dutch merchants.** Vines have grown in Vouvray at least since the Middle Ages, when the Church kept vineyards at local monasteries. In the 16th and 17th centuries Dutch merchants oversaw new plantings to supply London, Paris and [Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam) ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vouvray_%28wine%29)).
- **Where Chenin came from.** Chenin Blanc is thought to have originated in [Anjou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anjou_wine) around the 9th century before spreading to Vouvray ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vouvray_%28wine%29)).
- **One of the greatest wines ever.** In 2005 Decanter listed the 100 greatest wines ever made: Huet's 1947 Vouvray ranked sixth, the second-highest white after the 1921 [Château d'Yquem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teau_d'Yquem) ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domaine_Huet)).
- **Across the river.** Opposite Vouvray, across the [Loire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loire), lies [Montlouis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montlouis-sur-Loire), which also makes Chenin Blanc, usually with a little less acidity and concentration ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vouvray_%28wine%29)).

**Curious details**
- **Wild tulips.** The estate writes that each spring its vineyards were once covered with wild tulips, now a protected, endangered flower that survives on only a few dozen hectares of Vouvray vines ([Domaine Huet](https://www.domainehuet.com/?lang=EN)).
- **Cellars in the rock.** Le Mont sits directly above Huet's tuffeau cellars ([Domaine Huet](https://www.domainehuet.com/?lang=EN)). Tuffeau is the soft local limestone that built the Loire's [châteaux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teaux_of_the_Loire_Valley) ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuffeau_stone)).
- **A 9th-century wall.** The Clos du Bourg is still enclosed by a stone wall the estate dates to the 9th century ([Domaine Huet](https://www.domainehuet.com/?lang=EN)).
